feedback.a: Correct. That is the product definition, and the four elements it names are what you check on every agent review.
feedback.b: A schedule can start an agent, but a trigger is not the agent. An agent carries out adapting, multi-step work.
feedback.c: Too narrow. Agents combine instructions, knowledge, tools, and context, and can act across many connected systems.
feedback.d: That describes a connector. Connectors supply knowledge; the agent is what uses it.

feedback.a: Correct — target outcomes and behavioral rules.
feedback.b: Correct — the information available to the agent.
feedback.c: Correct — results produced and context retained during a run.
feedback.d: Not a building block. Cost matters operationally, but it is not part of the agent model.
feedback.e: Not a building block. That belongs to connectors and indexing, not the agent itself.

feedback.a: Correct. Fixed and repeatable with explicit control is exactly the Workflow mode case.
feedback.b: Auto mode determines its own path, so runs can vary. That is the opposite of what an auditor wants here.
feedback.c: They differ in a way that matters: Auto mode decides its own path, Workflow mode follows yours.
feedback.d: Agents can absolutely support auditable work — that is why Workflow mode and the lifecycle exist.

feedback.a: Correct on both halves. Content triggers fire on a change in a connected tool and hand the changed content to the agent as [[Trigger input]].
feedback.b: That requires a person to notice and paste, which defeats the point of automatic execution.
feedback.c: An input form needs a person to fill it in first, so it cannot start on its own.
feedback.d: A schedule fires on the clock, not on the change, and would miss or duplicate work.

feedback.a: Correct. It is a deliberate stricter access model for channel-wide visibility. To match web behavior, publish as visible only to the user with the option to share.
feedback.b: Not a defect. Permissions are enforced everywhere, but channel-wide visibility deliberately narrows which documents can be used.
feedback.c: Agents do not hold their own document grants. Access is evaluated at execution time against the relevant user or channel scope.
feedback.d: Retrieval still works in Slack. What changed is the set of documents the agent is allowed to draw on.

feedback.a: Correct. Broad audience, sensitive data, and write tools each independently call for a more robust process, and enterprise scope means comprehensive.
feedback.b: Reactive review after a broad launch is precisely what the lifecycle exists to prevent.
feedback.c: Process must scale with impact and data access — that is the explicit guidance.
feedback.d: Write tools are governed, not universally blocked. Admins choose which may run without confirmation, which is a reason for more review, not less.
